\[ S = \sum_{k=0}^{2026} k \binom{2k}{k} 2^k. \]

Compute the remainder when \( S \) is divided by 2027. (Note that 2027 is prime.)

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Let \(p=2027\) and \(m=\frac{p-1}{2}=1013\). Work modulo \(p\).

Define

\[
P(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\binom{2k}{k}x^k.
\]

Then

\[
S=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}k\binom{2k}{k}2^k
=\left. xP'(x)\right|_{x=2}.
\]

We first simplify \(P(x)\). For \(k>m\), the interval \(\{k+1,k+2,\dots,2k\}\) contains \(p\), while \(k!\) does not, so

\[
\binom{2k}{k}\equiv 0 \pmod p.
\]

For \(0\le k\le m\), using \(m\equiv -\frac12 \pmod p\),

\[
(-4)^k\binom{m}{k}
\equiv (-4)^k\frac{(-1/2)(-3/2)\cdots (-(2k-1)/2)}{k!}
=\frac{(2k)!}{(k!)^2}
=\binom{2k}{k}\pmod p.
\]

Hence

\[
P(x)\equiv \sum_{k=0}^{m}(-4)^k\binom{m}{k}x^k=(1-4x)^m \pmod p.
\]

Therefore

\[
S\equiv \left. x\frac{d}{dx}(1-4x)^m\right|_{x=2}
=-8m(1-8)^{m-1}
=-8m(-7)^{m-1}.
\]

Since \(m-1=1012\) is even,

\[
S\equiv -8\cdot 1013\cdot 7^{1012}\pmod{2027}.
\]

Now \(8\cdot 1013=8104\equiv -4\pmod{2027}\), so

\[
S\equiv 4\cdot 7^{1012}\pmod{2027}.
\]

By Euler’s criterion,

\[
7^{1013}\equiv \left(\frac{7}{2027}\right)\pmod{2027}.
\]

Using quadratic reciprocity,

\[
\left(\frac{7}{2027}\right)
=-\left(\frac{2027}{7}\right)
=-\left(\frac{4}{7}\right)
=-1.
\]

Thus \(7^{1013}\equiv -1\), so

\[
7^{1012}\equiv -7^{-1}\pmod{2027}.
\]

Since \(7\cdot 579=4053\equiv -1\pmod{2027}\), we have \(7^{1012}\equiv 579\). Hence

\[
S\equiv 4\cdot 579=2316\equiv 289\pmod{2027}.
\]

\[
\boxed{289}
\]
